_what: PINNED PREMISES AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT RETIRES EACH ONE.
_why: 2026-08-27/28: nine separate defects in one session were the same shape —
not a bug, but an assertion that outlived the condition it was written
under and kept asserting. A baseline control that forbade its own goal
state; a ceiling tiebreak pinned inert against a board that had changed
sources; a per-row guard that ran a whole-register health check because
the backlog happened to be zero the day it was written; a test pinning a
document this repo marks superseded; and a SessionStart hook whose author
matched it to when he NOTICED the problem rather than when it happens.
Recheck DATES chase the calendar. They cannot chase a CONDITION. A date
says 'look again on the 31st'; a condition says 'void the moment the
ceiling source changes'. Prose conditions decay — CLAUDE.md documents that
failure three times and then commits it again — so every condition here is
a NUMBER a probe measures from live state.
The one healthy example is the pattern being copied: ceiling_tiebreak's
08-17 note named, in writing, the condition that should retire it. When it
failed the failure explained itself and the fix took minutes.
_how_to_add: id        — kebab-case, stable; it is what a register row cites.
claim     — the premise IN THE FORM SOMEBODY ASSERTED IT. Not the fix.
where/anchor — the file the premise is load-bearing in, and a literal
string that must still appear in it. If the anchor vanishes
the code moved out from under the premise and the entry is
reported ANCHOR MOVED rather than silently checked against
something that is no longer there.
probe     — a key of draft/tools/premise_probes.js, returning a NUMBER.
holds_when — {op, value}: eq | ne | gt | gte | lt | lte.
note      — what to do when it goes VOID, for whoever reads the report.
_status: REPORT ONLY. --strict exits 1 on any VOID, for a caller that wants to gate.

premises.claim: RECENCY_WEIGHTS = (0.7, 0.3) is a defensible hand-set constant — the module's own words, 'a small gap means it was fine and we finally know it'
premises.note: VOID at QB: fitted optimum 0.333 against a shipped 0.7, mean rho gap 0.1154 against WR 0.0049 / TE 0.0074 / RB 0.0112 — a tenfold separation. NOT A LICENCE TO CHANGE THE WEIGHT: the constant is marked 'cannot be refit leak-free', so a fit that disagrees is evidence about the DECLARATION, not a replacement for it. Routed to E/Cory, register 386. This is the first premise here about the MODEL rather than about our hygiene, and it is the shape the rest should follow: what we SHIP, checked against what we FIT.
